newsitem.title: CHINA: China says oil output up sharply in January.
newsitem.headline: China says oil output up sharply in January.

text.p: China's production of oil rose markedly in January, with average daily output reaching 389,500 tonnes, the China National Petroleum Corp said. It gave no comparative figures.
China's average daily production of gas rose to 46.15 million cubic metres in January, it said, but gave no comparative figures.
China has set a production goal of 142 million tonnes of crude from onshore fields this year or 389,000 tonnes per day, higher than the 1996 figure, it said, without elaborating.
China produced a record 141 million tonnes of oil onshore and another 15 million tonnes offshore.
The first month's progress indicates a promising year in oil production, the Xinhua news agency quoted a senior official of the China National Petroleum Corp as saying.
Even ageing oilfields in eastern China, except for the Liaohe field that was hit by a heavy snowstorm in January, met production targets, he said.
The Shengli and Jilin fields exceeded state-set monthly.
Daqing, China's leading oilfield, produced 153,400 tonnes of crude a day in January, higher than the daily target.
